questions.question: Explain what fitness for purpose means when analysing an existing wheelchair ramp, and list the measurements you would take.
questions.expected_answer: Fitness for purpose asks whether the ramp does what its users need where it is used: a gradient a wheelchair user can climb, a width that fits a chair and helper, a non-slip surface, rails they can reach on both sides, landings to rest and a level landing at the door. Measurements: rise and length to calculate the gradient against the 1 in 12 limit, width against 1 200, rail height against 900 to 1 000 and whether rails extend past the ends, landing length against 1 200, and a test of the surface grip when wet.

questions.question: Compare concrete, steel and timber as materials for an outdoor ramp, giving a strength and a weakness of each, and name four safety hazards to look for.
questions.expected_answer: Concrete: strong, durable and can be brushed for grip, but heavy, needs a foundation and is slow to set. Steel: quick to prefabricate and erect, but rusts unless galvanised or painted and is slippery when smooth. Timber: warm and easy to work, good for handrails, but rots, splinters and is slippery when wet. Hazards: unequal risers, missing or gapped rails, no kerb on the ramp, water pooling on the surface, a landing too short at the door, chipped step nosings.

questions.question: Describe the layout of a written analysis of existing products and explain how it feeds into the design brief.
questions.expected_answer: For each product: a sketch or photograph with dimensions, a short description of what and where it is and who uses it, then a table with rows for fitness for purpose, materials, safety, cost, ergonomics, aesthetics and environmental impact, and columns for what was observed, the standard it is judged against, and the lesson for our design. Three or four different products are analysed. Each lesson becomes a specification or constraint in the brief, for example 1 in 12 or gentler, a level top landing, a brushed non-slip finish, rails on both sides, a kerb and galvanised fittings.
